chunk_findings.detail: `_orphan` sets `age = now - run.started_at` and then reports that age as when the run ended: `ended {_age(age)} ago`. A finished run has no end timestamp on `Run`, so a review that started 40 minutes ago and recorded `passed` 2 minutes ago is shown as "ended 40 min ago". The operator text in the intent ("ended 12 min ago") is therefore false for any run whose duration is non-trivial, and `started_at == 0` reports the run as having ended `now` seconds ago.

chunk_findings.detail: `busy |= _live_run_items(...)` treats every live registry pid as in-flight work, so idle and stall findings are suppressed for as long as that process exists. The required opposite check is only “alive and within its expected duration.” Given a rubber_duck run whose expected duration was 30 minutes, still alive at 2 hours with no lane progress, this lane is marked busy and is neither idle nor stalled, so the nudge ladder never fires. `_runs` also never reads expected duration off the marker, so inspect cannot apply that bound from these rows either.

chunk_findings.detail: Newest-run selection now uses `stamp = r.ended_at or r.started_at`. A finished run whose end is after a later run's start wins, so the orphan names the wrong gate. Given review pid 1 (`started_at=1000`, `ended_at=2000`, outcome `passed`) and pins pid 2 (`started_at=1500`, `ended_at=0`, no outcome), stamp 2000 beats 1500, so the lane is reported as waiting on the review that passed and the rerun command is `review`, even though the newest registry entry is the pins run that died with no outcome. The same ordering reports ORPHAN_WAIT while a newer live run is still in the registry whenever an older run's `ended_at` is greater than that live run's `started_at`.

chunk_findings.detail: The previous busy-forever defect is only partly fixed. `_live_run_items` still treats `m.expected_s <= 0` as in-flight for the whole life of the pid (`test_a_live_run_with_unknown_duration_is_live_work`: start + 100000s still returns `{"T1"}`). Given a live rubber_duck/ci marker with `expected_s` 0 and no lane progress for hours, `gather` still sets `busy` and never emits idle or stall, so the nudge ladder does not fire.

chunk_findings.detail: The knob documents a Claude Code range of 100000-1000000, with 0 meaning "leave the harness default", but `check=int_at_least(0)` accepts every other non-negative integer. Config `claude_autocompact_window=1` (or `2000000`) therefore loads, and doctor/health will name `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` at a value Claude Code's own range rejects, so the D-TE-Q2 alternative to rotation never actually compact the session.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/session.py:claude_autocompact_window

chunk_findings.detail: `handoff_note` claims the whole note is capped at `HANDOFF_NOTE_CHARS` (400), but the cap is applied only to the summary and the ellipsis is added outside the remaining budget. With `item_id="x"*359` (so `len(prefix)+len(suffix)==400`), any summary yields `budget==0` and the return value is 401 characters (`"…"` is still appended). With `item_id="x"*400`, `budget` is negative, the body collapses to `"…"`, and the note is 412+ characters and still ends with the suffix, so a 400-character brief paste drops `"; resume with \`ddflow brief\`."`.

chunk_findings.detail: `doctor_notes` reports only one auto-compact knob. Given `claude_autocompact_window=500000` and `claude_autocompact_pct_override=40` (the override that lowers the window), and usage below the rotate threshold, the note is only `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW=500000` and never mentions 40, so health/doctor tells the lead the full window is in effect.
